title: EEG Versus Neurofeedback
subtitle: Measurement is not training
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating eeg versus neurofeedback within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain eeg versus neurofeedback without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in eeg versus neurofeedback.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to eeg versus neurofeedback.

sections.explainSimply: EEG records electrical activity. Neurofeedback uses a selected signal feature to create a closed learning loop.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: A diagnostic or descriptive EEG answers a measurement question; neurofeedback adds real-time processing, a target rule and feedback intended to shape self-regulation.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Clinical EEG interpretation, QEEG analysis and neurofeedback protocol design require overlapping but non-identical competencies. A QEEG deviation does not automatically define a treatment target.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A driving instructor who gives immediate dashboard feedback while the learner practises a controllable skill.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand eeg versus neurofeedback to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Do not convert a colour map directly into a protocol.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using eeg versus neurofeedback predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Do not convert a colour map directly into a protocol. Evidence classification: established distinction.
